cases.name: absolution first person
cases.text: I absolve you from your sins in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

cases.name: absolution latin
cases.text: Ego te absolvo ab omnibus peccatis tuis.

cases.name: sins forgiven declaration
cases.text: Your sins are forgiven. Go in peace and sin no more.

cases.name: absolved declaration
cases.text: You are now absolved of everything you confessed today.

cases.name: consecration body
cases.text: Take this bread and eat it. This is my body, given for you.

cases.name: consecration latin
cases.text: Hoc est enim corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradetur.

cases.name: consecration blood
cases.text: Drink from this cup. This is my blood of the new covenant.

cases.name: ordination performed
cases.text: By the power given to me, I ordain you a priest forever.

cases.name: ordination pronouncement
cases.text: I now pronounce you ordained to the diaconate.

cases.name: imitation pope francis
cases.text: As Pope Francis would say, mercy is the bridge that connects God and man.

cases.name: imitation augustine
cases.text: Speaking as Saint Augustine, I tell you our hearts are restless by design.

cases.name: imitation aquinas
cases.text: As St. Thomas might say, grace builds on nature and does not destroy it.

cases.name: tao answer tao_1_1
cases.text: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.

cases.name: tao answer tao_8_1
cases.text: The highest excellence is like (that of) water. The excellence of water appears in its benefiting all things, and in its occupying, without striving (to the contrary), the low place which all men dislike. Hence (its way) is near to (that of) the Tao.

cases.name: tao answer tao_11_1
cases.text: The thirty spokes unite in the one nave; but it is on the empty space (for the axle), that the use of the wheel depends. Clay is fashioned into vessels; but it is on their empty hollowness, that their use depends. The door and windows are cut out (from the walls) to form an apartment; but it is on the empty space (within), that its use depends. Therefore, what has a (positive) existence serves for profitable adaptation, and what has not that for (actual) usefulness.

cases.name: tao answer tao_16_1
cases.text: The (state of) vacancy should be brought to the utmost degree, and that of stillness guarded with unwearying vigour. All things alike go through their processes of activity, and (then) we see them return (to their original state). When things (in the vegetable world) have displayed their luxuriant growth, we see each of them return to its root. This returning to their root is what we call the state of stillness; and that stillness may be called a reporting that they have fulfilled their appointed end.

cases.name: tao answer tao_37_1
cases.text: The Tao in its regular course does nothing (for the sake of doing it), and so there is nothing which it does not do.

cases.name: tao answer tao_43_1
cases.text: The softest thing in the world dashes against and overcomes the hardest; that which has no (substantial) existence enters where there is no crevice. I know hereby what advantage belongs to doing nothing (with a purpose).

cases.name: tao answer tao_60_1
cases.text: Governing a great state is like cooking small fish.

cases.name: tao answer tao_78_1
cases.text: There is nothing in the world more soft and weak than water, and yet for attacking things that are firm and strong there is nothing that can take precedence of it;--for there is nothing (so effectual) for which it can be changed.

borderline.name: quoting words of consecration to explain them
borderline.note: Explanatory quotation fed to the shared refuser. The refuser treats the shape as performance regardless of intent; that tradeoff is recorded here the same way the first exhibit records it.
borderline.text: The words of consecration are: This is my body, and, This is my blood.

borderline.name: quoting absolution formula in teaching
borderline.note: Teaching text quoting the formula, fed to the shared refuser. Same tradeoff as above.
borderline.text: In the confessional, the priest says the words I absolve you as the essential form of the sacrament.

borderline.name: attributed statement about Laozi
borderline.note: Attribution, not imitation. The text is traditionally attributed to Laozi (Lao Tzu), the Old Master, and a statement that reports that attribution is expected to pass through.
borderline.text: The Tao Te Ching is traditionally attributed to Laozi, who is said in its sixty-seventh chapter to hold three precious things: gentleness, economy, and shrinking from taking precedence of others.
